subject: Lighting inside and around cabinetry
hook: Kitchen lighting starts on the cabinet drawings.
ig:
Kitchen lighting starts on the cabinet drawings, not after the units are fitted.

Lighting inside and around cabinets is one of the easiest things to plan and one of the most awkward to add later. Cable holes, recesses and driver positions all need deciding before the panels are cut.

The five places to think about:
— under the wall units, lighting the worktop
— hidden profiles, so the light reads as a clean line
— plinths, for a soft evening glow
— inside tall larders and deep cupboards
— a reachable spot for each driver

Your electrician handles the wiring; our job is making sure the bespoke kitchen is designed with the routes and spaces ready for it.

Save this for your kitchen plans, and tap the link in bio to book a design consultation.
fb:
March is when a lot of people start planning a new kitchen — and lighting is the bit most often left too late.

Under-cabinet strips, plinth lights, lights inside the larder: they all need cable routes and spaces built into the units before anything is cut. Swipe through for the five places to plan it, and the one detail almost everyone forgets (where the driver goes).

We design bespoke kitchens with you and make them in our Hanley workshop, with the routes ready for your electrician.
